    - heading "Understand Symmetry Explorer" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "A symmetry explorer tests whether a shape matches itself after a reflection, rotation, or translation. In Symmetry Explorer, that statement is the exact rule used on the labelled chart and in the three numerical examples. A useful rule is Symmetry mapping: T(shape)=shape. You can learn Symmetry Explorer by trying one small example instead of long theory."
    - paragraph: Choose a possible symmetry. Apply the transformation. Check whether every image point lands on the original shape. Try the example below. Write your steps and choose an answer before opening the comparison.
    - paragraph: "In real life, mirror design: A butterfly-like design can have line symmetry. Watch out: Calling a near visual match a symmetry. Symmetry needs an exact match."

  - article:
    - heading "Key Ideas" [level=2]
    - paragraph: A figure has line symmetry if it matches itself after a reflection about a line (mirror line). It has rotational symmetry of order n if it matches itself after a rotation of 360°/n about a center.
    - heading "Rules & Formulas" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "› Rotational angle: θ = 360°/n"
    - paragraph: "› Order from angle: n = 360°/θ"
    - paragraph: "› Line symmetry test: After reflecting across the line, every point of the image coincides with a point of the original."
    - paragraph: "› Invariants under isometries: distance, angle, perimeter, and area remain unchanged."
  - article:
    - heading "Worked Example" [level=2]
    - text: "Example: Equilateral triangle"
    - paragraph:
      - text: "• Mirror lines: 3"
      - text: (each median)
      - text: "• Rotational order: n = 3"
      - text: "• Angle of rotation: θ = 360°/3 = 120°"
      - text: "• Center of rotation: O(0,0)"
    - generic: Matches after every 120° rotation and across any median.
  - heading "Common Misconception" [level=2]
  - paragraph: Rotational symmetry is about a center, not a line. A figure can have no line symmetry but still have rotational symmetry. Always check both separately.
  - heading "Try It! Mini Challenge" [level=2]
  - paragraph: Test your understanding
